Hon'ble Siddharth,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A for the State.
Learned A.G.A informs that notice has been served on opposite party no. 2, but no one has turned up to oppose this bail application.

There are allegations against the applicant of abduction of minor girl with intent to marry,
commission of offences of rape, penetrative sexual assault, criminal intimidation and offence under Section 3(2)(5) of SC/ST Act has also been made.

sentences.text: 1 Counsel for the applicant submits that the victim has claimed her age as 23 years in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C and in her ossification test report her age has been found to be 16 to 18 years.
Counsel for the applicant also submits that given margin of two years on the higher side, she can be considered to be major.
The victim in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C has admitted eloping with the applicant and going to Gujarat and other places.
She has stated that the applicant assured her of marriage.

However, in the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.,
she has made allegation of commission of offence of rape against the applicant but has refused to get her internal medical examination conducted.
There is no corroborative medical evidence of the allegations made against the applicant by the victim.
She has falsely implicated the applicant in this case.
The applicant is in jail since 15.08.2023 and has no criminal history to his credit.
The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant, Pankaj Yadav, involved in Case Crime No. 319 of 2023, under Sections- 363, 366,
376, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(5) of SC/ST Act, Police Station- Turkpatti, District- Kushinagar, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or threaten the witnesses.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed, either personally or as directed by the Court.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) In case the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence,
proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the Court on Pankaj Yadav vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159352427/

(v) The applicant shall remain present in person before the Trial Court on the dates fixed for (i)
opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause,
then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
In case, of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

considering the dictum of Apex Court in the case of Satendra Kumar Antil vs. C.B.I., passed in S.L.P (Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021; considering 5-6 times overcrowding in jails over and above their capacity by the under trials and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
